notes:
- Spoilers pair with their own closing tag, and carry a label: The site's inline span and block div spoiler forms are read alongside the older div rel=spoiler. An opening pairs with its closest matching close by tag depth, labels are trimmed or dropped when invalid, and what is behind the lid is parsed as full Markdown up to three nested lids.
- Five GIF indexes, and Tenor says when it has been retired: Klipy and GIPHY join Safebooru, nekos.best and Tenor, and Settings now names the index a search goes to. Each key is stored encrypted on its own, a keyed provider without a key falls back to the anonymous booru, and Tenor's refusal now says its public API was retired in 2026.
- The drift reaches the floor, and then stops growing: The heap now gathers on the screen's real bottom edge and passes behind the floating bar instead of stopping at the bar's outer top and leaving a gap. Deposits leave headroom for the columns beside them and each landing compacts the heap, so it settles at a stable depth rather than growing into a wall; the low-end tier still compacts, just without the smoothing pass.
- The navigation bar catches the snow: A winter sky leaves a wavy cap along the pill's real capsule, short drips over its face and a slow sparkle. Its thickness follows the heap below it, it breathes on the sky's own clock, and it is drawn after the bar. The drift is no longer lifted to the bar's padded outer edge.
- The shapes have more to see, and the fall has depth: Sakura gained a five-petal blossom, clover a three-leaf variant, powder a shaded crescent, and the crystal plate twelve spokes with a faceted needle. Larger shapes are brighter, faster and in front; each answers a gust differently; the underside of a turn is dimmed; and the fall eases into the bottom of the screen.
- Fewer allocations and redraws under the same sky: The sky reuses one path and one placement object for every particle in a frame, the drift reuses its ink and scratch paths, resting glyphs follow the quality tier, and smoothing runs only after something has landed.
- The bar arrives as a surface, and a press lets go when the finger does: The bar grows into place with a short spring scale and shrinks slightly on the way out. A press follows the finger that started it, so a second finger can no longer keep a control squashed after the first has lifted.
- Fireflies and starlight are gone, and everything falls: The two glowing shapes were the only ones that rose; at the size a particle is drawn neither is a shape you can name. Summer is now the dandelion seed, which comes down under its parachute. An install that had fireflies or starlight selected wakes up on snow rather than a blank sky.
- Leaves turn over as they come down: Petals, leaves and seeds are drawn squeezed across their own axis as they rotate, so a maple shows its underside instead of winding round like a clock hand. How far a shape rolls is a property of the shape.
- The autumn leaves redrawn: Maple, oak and ginkgo margins are now curves sampled from a width function with tangent-continuous joints, palmate veins and a lit rim. Maple comes in amber, orange and red; sakura gained a curled inner face; the dandelion's filaments bow both ways.
- Three more winter skies, and a quality that picks itself: Powder, Crystal and Needles join Snow, and a new Quality row decides how many flakes are drawn, how often the clock steps and whether a flake keeps its branches. Auto reads this phone's memory and core count the first time you switch the sky on.
- Settling and wind wait to be asked - and the wind now works on a still page: The drift and the reaction to scrolling sit behind their own switches. An ambient breeze runs underneath the gestures, a drag and its fling count once, and the drift spreads instead of growing spikes.
